_meta.description: Full 30-question RAGAS evaluation, run twice on Kaggle GPU per kaggle/README.md, judge model qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0, embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2. Real production runs (not the earlier n=2 local validation). Run 2 used max_workers=1 (fully serial) to test whether concurrency was causing the answer_relevancy NaN failure seen in Run 1 - it did not fix it, disproving that hypothesis (see LOG.md 'Phase 8 follow-up 2'). Full per-question response/context text is not stored here (some rows are very large, one pathologically so in Run 1 - see known_issues); scores are the complete real record for Run 1. Run 2's per-question detail was not captured (only console summary), only its mean_scores are recorded.
known_issues: Faithfulness varied substantially between runs: 0.8679 (Run 1) vs 0.6555 (Run 2), a ~0.21 swing on the same 30-question set. LLM generation is non-deterministic, so some run-to-run variance is expected, but this magnitude means a single run's faithfulness score should not be cited as a fixed property of the system - see LOG.md and results/writeup.md Section 7.3.

Run 1 only: JPM-1's generated answer degenerated into a multi-thousand-character repetition loop (a known small/quantized-model failure mode). Corrupted faithfulness/context_precision for that row (both NaN); context_recall was unaffected since it doesn't depend on the generated response.

Custom '_id'/'_ticker' tracking columns added when building the RAGAS dataset were silently dropped by EvaluationDataset - Run 1's per-question rows below are matched to test-set IDs by position (processing order matches data/eval/ragas_test_set.json's question order), not by an explicit ID RAGAS preserved.

RESOLVED in run_3 (local): answer_relevancy NaN was root-caused to qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0 being an unreliable judge specifically for AnswerRelevancy's noncommittal classification sub-task on real multi-point answers - not a concurrency or environment bug as first suspected (that theory was tested directly and disproven with OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1, which had zero effect). Fixed by giving AnswerRelevancy its own stronger judge (qwen2.5:14b) while leaving the other 3 metrics on the faster 7b judge. See LOG.md Phase 8 follow-up 4.

notes: answer_relevancy is finally non-NaN for all 30 questions here - see LOG.md Phase 8 follow-up 4 for the full root-cause story (qwen2.5:7b-instruct-q4_0 was systematically misclassifying real multi-point answers as noncommittal in AnswerRelevancy specifically; swapping just that one metric to qwen2.5:14b as judge fixed it, confirmed directly by isolated before/after testing on the same real response).
2 of 30 rows (both the MD&A-trends question, not risk-factors) still scored answer_relevancy=0.0 even with the 14b judge - a residual, disclosed error rate rather than a total failure.

One unrelated OutputParserException hit Faithfulness json parsing for one PG question mid-run (job 51/120) - ragas caught it and continued (raise_exceptions=False), resulting in 1 NaN context_recall value; did not affect answer_relevancy.

Full local run took 2h43m on the user's own GPU (vs ~20-36 min per run on Kaggle GPU for earlier attempts) - this run intentionally traded speed for local control after two Kaggle runs failed to produce a usable answer_relevancy.
